# Units, rates and speeds (v3.70)

*Generated by `node tools/units_page.mjs --out docs/UNITS_AND_RATES.md`. Do not edit by hand: the table is read out of `units.js`, and `--check` fails if this page has drifted from the code.*

Until v3.70 every rate and speed in this app was a bare number in a parameter block, and the conversion between ticks, hours, seconds and metres was written out by hand wherever it was needed. Three models each did it their own way. This page is the first place all of them are listed together, and listing them together is what made five disagreements visible.

**This release changes no behaviour.** Every value below is a copy of a literal that is still where it was, so every run, run id, fixture and pinned digest is exactly what it was. Adopting the conversions at the call sites is a later, separately gated step, one site at a time.

## What listing them together showed

### Two models declare a different number of ticks per hour under the same name

flowsim.js declares 60 (a tick is a minute); wms.js declares 4 (a tick is a quarter hour). Neither reads the other.

Entries: `flowsim.ticksPerHour`, `wms.ticksPerHour`

### The two travel speeds in the app differ by a factor of about 206

The animation moves a unit at 0.35 cells/tick, which is 0.35 m/min or about 0.0058 m/s. The pick-travel model walks at 1.2 m/s, which is 72 m/min. 72 / 0.35 is 205.71428571428572. Reconciling them would change behaviour, so v3.70 states it and changes nothing.

Entries: `flowsim.cellsPerTick`, `simulation.pickerSpeedMps`

### A conveyor has no speed

It is geometry that reshapes a path, plus a dimensionless count multiplier capped at 2.2, plus a units/hour figure with no length. Nothing in the app converts a belt length and a band speed into a transit time.

Entries: `domain.conveyor.unitsPerHr`, `flowsim.autoBoostPerLane`, `flowsim.autoFactorMax`

### A declared transporter speed is never read

library.js accepts metres per second for a custom transporter, stores it and prints it. No simulation consumes it.

Entries: `library.transporter.speedMps`

### The arrival band's coefficient of variation has two values that differ in the last digit

1.3 - 0.7 is 0.6000000000000001 in IEEE-754, so computing the coefficient from the endpoints gives 0.17320508075688776 while the exact-variance route gives 0.17320508075688773. Only the second squares back to exactly 0.03. Which form a caller uses decides whether its arithmetic round-trips.

Entries: `flowsim.arrivalCv.fromEndpoints`, `flowsim.arrivalCv.fromVariance`

### Service time has no variability at all

The serving loop adds a rate to an accumulator and releases whole units; there is no service-time distribution, so the coefficient of variation of service is zero by construction. The arrival ripple is the only variability the model has.

Entries: `flowsim.spawnNoiseLo`, `flowsim.spawnNoiseHi`

## The registry

A value is **cited**, a **teaching** value, or **measured** on a named source with its n. Nothing is unlabelled. A teaching value is a number chosen so the model is instructive; it is not a measurement of any plant.

### domain.js

| Entry | Value | Unit | Kind | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `domain.metresPerCell` | 1 | m | teaching | Metres per grid cell |

- **`domain.metresPerCell`** — Because a cell is a metre and a tick a minute, cells/tick reads directly as m/min.

### domain.js ELEMENTS

| Entry | Value | Unit | Kind | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `domain.agv.movesPerHr` | 30 | units/hr | teaching | Automated guided vehicle moves |
| `domain.asrs.cycleSec` | 45 | s/unit | teaching | AS/RS cycle |
| `domain.conveyor.unitsPerHr` | 180 | units/hr | teaching | Conveyor throughput |
| `domain.mfgSource.emitRatePerHr` | 120 | units/hr | teaching | Emit rate of a manufacturing source |
| `domain.rgv.movesPerHr` | 60 | units/hr | teaching | Rail-guided vehicle moves |
| `domain.shuttle.cycleSec` | 28 | s/unit | teaching | Shuttle cycle |

- **`domain.conveyor.unitsPerHr`** — A throughput with no length and no velocity. A conveyor's band speed does not exist in this model.
- **`domain.mfgSource.emitRatePerHr`** — Found by the source scan below rather than by hand - which is the scan earning its keep on its first run.

### flowsim.js PARAMS

| Entry | Value | Unit | Kind | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flowsim.arrivalCv.fromEndpoints` | 0.17320508075688776 | share | teaching | Arrival coefficient of variation, computed from the band endpoints |
| `flowsim.arrivalCv.fromVariance` | 0.17320508075688773 | share | teaching | Arrival coefficient of variation, computed from the exact variance |
| `flowsim.autoBoostPerLane` | 0.12 | x | teaching | Travel-speed lift per automation lane |
| `flowsim.autoFactorMax` | 2.2 | x | teaching | Cap on the automation travel multiplier |
| `flowsim.cellsPerTick` | 0.35 | cells/tick | teaching | Base travel speed of a moving unit |
| `flowsim.congestQueueThreshold` | 6 | count | teaching | Queue length at which a bench is called congested |
| `flowsim.minLineThroughput` | 8 | units/hr | teaching | Floor on line throughput so a sparse layout still animates |
| `flowsim.minStationServicePerTick` | 0.02 | units/tick | teaching | Floor on a station's service rate |
| `flowsim.shipDwellTicks` | 8 | ticks | teaching | Dwell at the outbound dock before a unit retires |
| `flowsim.spawnNoiseHi` | 1.3 | x | teaching | Upper bound of the per-tick arrival ripple |
| `flowsim.spawnNoiseLo` | 0.7 | x | teaching | Lower bound of the per-tick arrival ripple |
| `flowsim.ticksPerHour` | 60 | count | teaching | Ticks that stand for one hour in the flow simulation |

- **`flowsim.arrivalCv.fromEndpoints`** — 0.17320508075688776. Its square is 0.03000000000000001, not 0.03, because 1.3 - 0.7 is 0.6000000000000001 in IEEE-754.
- **`flowsim.arrivalCv.fromVariance`** — 0.17320508075688773. This one squares back to exactly 0.03 and satisfies sqrt(3) x cv === 0.3 exactly; the endpoint form does neither. Which form a caller uses decides whether its arithmetic round-trips.
- **`flowsim.autoBoostPerLane`** — A dimensionless count multiplier, not a conveyor speed. A conveyor has no speed in this model.
- **`flowsim.cellsPerTick`** — 0.35 m/min, about 0.0058 m/s. simulation.js walks its picker at 1.2 m/s (72 m/min), about 206 times faster. The two models have never been reconciled; this note is the first place the app says so.
- **`flowsim.minStationServicePerTick`** — A floor of 50 ticks per unit, so a bench always eventually drains its queue.
- **`flowsim.spawnNoiseLo`** — The whole of the arrival variability this model has. Service has none at all.
- **`flowsim.ticksPerHour`** — wms.js declares 4 for the same word - a quarter-hour bucket. The two models do not share this constant and never did.

## The conversions

Each one is written in the **same order** as the expression it stands for, because floating-point arithmetic is not associative: `cap * (1/tph)` is not `cap / tph`. A caller adopts one only where equality has been proven on real values.

| Conversion | Reads | Worked value |
|---|---|---|
| `perTick(unitsPerHr, ticksPerHour)` | units per hour to units per tick | 65.8 at 60 gives 1.0966666666666667 |
| `ticksPerUnit(unitsPerTick)` | a rate to the ticks one unit costs | 0.02 gives 50 |
| `secondsPerUnit(unitsPerHr)` | units per hour to seconds per unit | 45 gives 80 |
| `unitsPerHrFromSeconds(sec)` | a cycle time to units per hour | 30 gives 120 |
| `minutesPerTick(ticksPerHour)` | how long a tick is | 60 gives 1, 4 gives 15 |
| `takt(shiftSec, demandPerShift)` | the takt time of a line | 28800 over 480 gives 60 s |
| `to(quantity, unit)` | any conversion inside one dimension, refused across two | 0.35 cells/tick is 0.005833333333333333 m/s |

A conversion across dimensions is **refused by name** rather than silently scaled: asking for a rate in metres per second raises *refusing to convert units/hr (rate) to m/s (speed)*.

## What is deliberately not adopted

Two sites keep their literal and will keep it, and the reason is floating point rather than taste.

- **wms.js capTick** — The stage loop multiplies a capacity by a precomputed 1/ticksPerHour. In floating point cap x (1/tph) is not cap / tph, and the arrival and capacity chains both depend on the existing order. The conversion is declared here and the literal stays.
- **flowsim.js arrival ripple** — Re-expressing 0.7 + 0.6u as 1 + (2u - 1) x 0.3 is equal by algebra and unequal in floating point for most generator outputs, first at the very first draw. The literal stays character for character; a declared coefficient of variation is a different run with a different id, never the same run re-expressed.

## What the source scan reports, and what it cannot see

`unregistered(source)` scans a module's text for rate-shaped declarations and reports the ones the registry does not carry. It reads **names**, so a rate called something unexpected can hide from it. On its first run it found one real omission — a manufacturing source's emit rate that had been missed by hand — and two things that are correctly not entries:

- **`throughputOrdersPerHour`** in wms.js — An accumulator initialised to 0, not a declared rate. The scan reads names, so it cannot tell the difference; this list is where that limit is admitted.
- **`labourPerHour`** in analytics.js — A cost in euros per hour, not a speed. Costs are deliberately outside this registry - analytics.defaultRates owns them and says so.

## Honesty

> Every rate and speed in this app, with its unit and where it came from. A value is cited, a teaching value, or measured on a named source with its n - never unlabelled. The conversions are exact arithmetic written in the same order as the expressions they stand for, because floating-point arithmetic is not associative; a caller adopts one only where equality has been proven on real values, and the one site where it cannot be is named. The registry is AUTHORITATIVE BY DECLARATION AND ASSERTED BY A HARNESS, not enforced by a compiler: this repository has no build step, so verify_units.js compares the registry with the live modules and fails when they drift. A rate belongs to a bench, a step or a shift - never to a person - and a utilisation computed from one may not be read as an individual's performance (BetrVG 87(1)6, GDPR Art. 88).

## Reproduce

```sh
node tools/units_page.mjs --check
node verify_units.js
```
